BiblicalUsage: The word appears once: Peter tells Cornelius, 'Therefore came I unto you without gainsaying, as soon as I was sent for.' It is the adverb for coming at once, without arguing or objecting — Peter did not dispute the vision, did not argue with the messengers, but came as soon as he was sent for.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for without gainsaying carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is Peter's obedience — he came as soon as he was sent for, without arguing.
